geometry_proposal.use_as: unsurveyed sensitivity from the current published anchor-preserving chord selection; retain operational stops and recalculate service and costs; the existing ring line is held unchanged for a separate square-ring study

service_basis: Current source-published Baghdad planning seed; apply the same service optimizer, demand and cost method to both cases, and explicitly apply the same powered-axle research family to all fourteen lines. Derived runtime, dwell, fleet, quantities and cost may differ.
open_assumptions: The city demand, population and route inputs are planning estimates, not a surveyed forecast or right-of-way.
All fourteen lines use the same powered-axle research family. The model has no physically supported available-force map, so no physical journey or propulsion acceptance is demonstrated.
The 20 m value is a route-geometry screening tolerance only; it is not a clearance, survey or engineering limit.
Thirteen radial routes are simplified while preserving their operational stops; the closed ring line is unchanged and is not evaluated as a square-ring candidate.
Civil classes, right-of-way, crossings, utilities, ground conditions and prices are Class C model assumptions, not site evidence or quotations.

The baseline is the current published anchor-preserving chord selection, not the seed's original 513 km geometry. No route, station, propulsion system, physical candidate, engineering, manufacturing, operating or movement-authority selection is made.
